title: Prompt Interference in LLM Post-Training: Why Pass@k Optimization Can Degrade Pass@1
abstract: arXiv:2602.21189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Pass@$k$ is a widely used performance metric for verifiable large language model tasks, including mathematical reasoning, code generation, and short-answer reasoning. It defines success if any of $k$ independently sampled solutions passes a verifier. This multi-sample inference metric has motivated inference-aware fine-tuning methods that directly optimize pass@$k$. However, prior work reports a trade-off: pass@$k$ improves while pass@1 degrades under such methods. This trade-off is practically important because pass@1 often remains a hard operational constraint due to latency and cost budgets, imperfect verifier coverage, and the need for a reliable single-shot fallback. translated_title: 大语言模型后训练中的提示干扰：为什么Pass@k优化会降低Pass@1
translated_abstract: Pass@$k$是可验证大语言模型任务（包括数学推理、代码生成和简答题推理）中广泛使用的性能指标。其定义为：如果$k$个独立采样的解决方案中任意一个通过验证器，即视为成功。这种多样本推理指标推动了一系列推理感知微调方法的发展，这些方法直接优化pass@$k$。然而，先前的研究报告了一种权衡现象：在此类方法下，pass@$k$提升的同时pass@1却出现下降。这一权衡在实践中非常重要，因为受延迟和成本预算、验证器覆盖不完善，以及需要可靠的单次推理兜底等因素影响，pass@1往往仍然是一个硬性的运营约束。我们研究了这种权衡的根源，并对pass@$k$策略优化何时会通过提示干扰引发的梯度冲突降低pass@1给出了理论刻画。这种干扰源于共享的模型参数将不同提示耦合在一起（原文此处被截断）
tldr: 本文揭示了LLM后训练中直接优化pass@k反而会降低pass@1的根源——共享模型参数导致的“提示干扰”会引发梯度冲突，并对这一现象何时发生给出了理论刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a theoretical characterization of why pass@k policy optimization can degrade pass@1 in LLM post-training, showing that prompt interference—caused by shared model parameters coupling different prompts—induces gradient conflicts.
